notes: The source half of the macOS V8 supply chain. It pins IDENTITY -- which
rusty_v8, which V8, which gn, which targets -- and deliberately does not pin
gn arguments. android-v8.lock.json and ohos-v8.lock.json do not either: the
argument list is exported by the build recipe and recorded into each
component-manifest.json's `normalized_gn_args` by the manifest writer, so it
is a description of what a real build used rather than a claim typed here in
advance. windows-v8.lock.json is the exception and says why in its own notes:
that target cross-compiles to a DLL and pins the arguments because the shape
of the artifact depends on them.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: hashes. A component-manifest.json carries the
sha256 of real bytes, and those bytes do not exist until a macOS runner has
built them -- .github/workflows/apple-v8-probe.yml exists to establish what
that build costs and which arguments it accepts before a recipe is written
against guesses. The Apple ANGLE round made the price of skipping that step
explicit: its probe ran first, the recipe was written against measured facts,
and the round still needed four lane iterations, every one of which found a
defect only a real build could reveal.
iOS is not here, and that is a decision rather than an omission. On iOS the
content JavaScript runs in WKWebView's WebContent process to get the system
JIT -- an embedded V8 there would be interpreted, which is the arrangement
the project already rejected for in-process JavaScriptCore. macOS is the one
Apple platform with no architectural obstacle to in-process V8: the public
hardened-runtime entitlement allows JIT.
The same gn source, revision and patch set the Android and OpenHarmony
builds pin. The BINARY cannot be shared with them -- theirs is a Linux
executable and this recipe runs on macOS -- so what is pinned here is the
source identity the macOS binary must also have been built from.
The patch is named for gcc and is still listed for macOS on purpose: it is
part of the pinned gn identity, and a gn built from a different patch set is
a different gn no matter which compiler ignored the warning it suppresses.
Whether Apple's clang needs the suppression is not the question; whether
this is the same gn is.
Derived from contracts/apple/deployment-floor.json's macos platform entry,
not chosen here. That file is the single source for every Apple deployment
target and scripts/test-apple-deployment-floor-contract.sh fails the build
when a consumer carries its own copy of the number -- this entry exists so
the V8 recipe has something to pass to the compiler, and it is checked
against the contract rather than trusted.
It matters for a reason with no build step to land in: an archive built
without an explicit deployment target inherits the runner's own macOS
version as its floor. That links on the runner and fails on a consumer's
older Mac, which is the same shape as the ANGLE loader-path trap -- correct
everywhere the project can see, wrong where it cannot.

targets_notes: The baselines are the same conservative pair every other platform's lock
carries, and that is deliberate. This field states the MINIMUM a consumer's
CPU must satisfy, not a description of the machine that built the archive.
It would be easy to write something higher and plausible here: macOS 11 runs
on Apple silicon from the M1 up and on Intel Macs from roughly Haswell, so
every supported machine does in fact have NEON, SSE4.2 and POPCNT. But
whether the ARCHIVE requires them is a question about what the compiler
emitted, and nothing has compiled it yet. Raising a baseline is a claim about
bytes; it belongs in the same change as the bytes.
